findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the material_basis value written on the fully-pinned PASS/FAIL composite path (alongside the already-defined 'basis_unavailable' and 'error_unpinned'), so the marker vocabulary is complete and the AC4 test can assert the pinned basis.
evidence: Plan defines fallback markers: 'the fingerprint falls back to the existing plan material fingerprint plus a `basis_unavailable` marker' and ERROR '`material_basis: "error_unpinned"`'

AC4-adjacent: a prior review round already asked to assert 'that material_basis is the pinned (non-fallback) basis' — implying the pinned value name is used by tests/consumers but is never spelled out in the plan
No plan text names the material_basis value for the fully-pinned composite (e.g. 'pinned' / 'composite')
findings.finding: material_basis functions as a reader-consumed marker vocabulary but the plan defines only the fallback values ('basis_unavailable', 'error_unpinned') and never names the value written on the normal pinned PASS/FAIL success path.
findings.location: Fix plan / 'Required fingerprint shape' and 'Acceptance criteria mapping' (material_basis field)
scenarios: A consumer or the AC4 regression test needs to assert the pinned (non-fallback) basis but the plan gives it no literal to check against
Longitudinal gate analysis distinguishing pinned vs fallback vs error eras cannot enumerate the full material_basis vocabulary
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit pinned-basis literal (e.g. material_basis: "pinned") to the Required fingerprint shape section and enumerate the full {pinned, basis_unavailable, error_unpinned} vocabulary.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate every emit_gate_error/build_gate_error_payload reference via find_referencing_symbols (plan_review gate_dispatch.py:139,:213; code_review :412,:570; completion :687, completion_failures.py:227), and specify that the completion ERROR stamp is gated to gate=='completion' so plan_review/code_review ERROR records are provably untouched.
evidence: Plan: 'src/rebar/llm/gate_error_sidecar.py: stamp completion ERROR records with best-effort material_fingerprint, material_basis, and verifier_version without changing error propagation.'
gate_error_sidecar.py:31-35 — _GATE_EVENT_TYPE maps plan_review, code_review, and completion; build_gate_error_payload(gate, ...) and emit_gate_error(gate, ...) are gate-agnostic and shared.

emit_gate_error call sites (grep + symbol sweep): plan_review at gate_dispatch.py:139 and :213; code_review at :412 and :570; completion at :687 and completion_failures.py:227 — none of the six are enumerated by the plan.

The plan enriches build_gate_error_payload/emit_gate_error but the payload builder currently takes no gate-conditional branch (gate_error_sidecar.py:38-56), so an unconditional stamp would land on plan_review/code_review REVIEW_RESULT gate_error records too.
findings.finding: The plan scopes gate_error_sidecar.py to 'stamp completion ERROR records with material_fingerprint/material_basis/verifier_version', but build_gate_error_payload and emit_gate_error are SHARED symbols serving plan_review, code_review, AND completion (via _GATE_EVENT_TYPE at gate_error_sidecar.py:31-35). The plan's affected-reference inventory names only the file and the completion case; it omits the completion ERROR call sites it must gate to and the non-completion call sites that an unconditional builder change would affect.
findings.location: Scope / file impact: 'src/rebar/llm/gate_error_sidecar.py: stamp completion ERROR records ... without changing error propagation.' and Required fingerprint shape: 'For completion gate_error_v1 ERROR sidecars ...'
scenarios: gate_dispatch.py:687 (emit_gate_error(ticket_id, 'completion', ...)) — a completion ERROR path the plan does not name; if the enrichment is threaded only through completion_failures.py:227 it would be missed here, leaving this ERROR record unstamped.
completion_failures.py:227 (bounded-recovery completion ERROR) — the plan's ERROR discussion does not name this specific completion emit site, so the version/fingerprint stamp could silently omit it.

gate_dispatch.py:139/:213 (plan_review) and :412/:570 (code_review) — if build_gate_error_payload/emit_gate_error are enriched unconditionally, verifier_version/material_basis leak onto plan_review and code_review ERROR records, an out-of-scope schema change the plan claims is completion-only.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a gate-conditional branch in build_gate_error_payload (or a completion-only emitter wrapper) keyed on gate=='completion', and name both completion ERROR call sites (gate_dispatch.py:687, completion_failures.py:227) plus the four excluded plan_review/code_review sites in the scope, deriving the list from find_referencing_symbols rather than the file name alone.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen the FAIL-sidecar regression assertion to verify the pinned composite: that material_basis is the pinned (non-fallback) basis and that the fingerprint changes when the completion_read_basis receipt digest or prefetch manifest identifiers change, not merely that it is non-null.
evidence: 'A regression test asserts a FAIL sidecar carries a non-null fingerprint and version.'

Fix plan: 'Fallbacks are explicit and era-visible: if a legacy/local caller has no completion read basis, the fingerprint falls back to the existing plan material fingerprint plus a basis_unavailable marker'
A non-null oracle cannot distinguish the pinned composite (plan_material_fingerprint + completion_read_basis + prefetch manifest) from a degraded plan-material-only fallback.
findings.finding: The regression test (AC4) asserts only a non-null fingerprint and version on a FAIL sidecar, but the fingerprint has several fallback branches (basis_unavailable, error_unpinned, plan-material-only). A non-null assertion passes even when the fingerprint degraded to a fallback that omits the pinned completion_read_basis receipt digest and prefetch manifest — the very inputs the plan says make FAIL->PASS attributable. The test would go green without proving the composite actually incorporates the run-specific inputs.
findings.location: Verification plan step 1 / AC4 ('asserts non-null fingerprint and version')
scenarios: A FAIL sidecar emitted with a basis_unavailable fallback fingerprint would satisfy AC4 while carrying none of the ticket-comments/evidence-set identity that motivates the ticket — the gap the plan exists to close would remain, undetected by the test.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test case with a fully pinned completion_read_basis + prefetch manifest that asserts material_basis is the pinned value and that mutating the receipt_digest / prefetch identifier yields a different material_fingerprint, in addition to the non-null check.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly what fingerprint/material_basis a deterministic precheck-FAIL sidecar (no LLM run, no completion_read_basis, no prefetch manifest — gate_ops.py:105-112) carries, and confirm it is non-null per AC4 (e.g. plan material fingerprint + a `precheck_fail_unpinned`/`basis_unavailable` marker).
evidence: gate_ops.py:105-112 returns a deterministic FAIL verdict (`run_verify: False`) for an oversize description or failed child-closure gate; this verdict never reaches completion_reconcile and carries no `completion_read_basis`
completion_prefetch's manifest is only produced on the LLM-run path (gate_ops.py:200), so a no-LLM precheck FAIL has no prefetch identifiers
plan's fallback text frames the basis-absent case as 'if a legacy/local caller has no completion read basis' — not the deterministic-precheck FAIL where no verifier ran
AC4 asserts 'a FAIL sidecar carries a non-null fingerprint' without distinguishing the deterministic-precheck FAIL from the LLM FAIL
findings.finding: The fingerprint mechanism does not explicitly cover the deterministic precheck-FAIL passthrough path, where no LLM ran and both completion_read_basis and the prefetch manifest are absent — a common FAIL variant that AC1/AC4 require to carry a non-null fingerprint.
findings.location: Fix plan -> Required fingerprint shape (fallbacks) / AC1 / AC4
scenarios: An oversize-description or unmet child-closure precheck produces a deterministic FAIL sidecar with no read basis and no prefetch manifest
The AC4 regression test happens to exercise an LLM FAIL and passes, while deterministic-precheck FAILs silently fall to a fingerprint the plan never pinned down

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the fingerprint and material_basis assigned to a deterministic precheck-FAIL sidecar (no LLM run, no completion_read_basis, no prefetch manifest), mapping it explicitly to one of the fallback tiers.
evidence: close_precheck.py:405 emits the deterministic precheck-FAIL verdict through the same completion_sidecar.emit() the plan enriches

completion_precheck_output.schema.json:11 — precheck emits a 'deterministic FAIL completion_verdict' with no verifier inputs (no plan material fingerprint, no completion_read_basis, no prefetch manifest)

Plan fallback tiers cover 'legacy/local caller has no completion read basis' -> basis_unavailable, 'no ticket material at all' -> best-effort/unknown, and ERROR -> error_unpinned, but the deterministic-precheck-FAIL (a normal FAIL verdict lacking ALL verifier inputs) is not explicitly mapped to a tier
findings.finding: The deterministic precheck-FAIL sidecar (child-closure finding, no LLM run, no completion_read_basis, no prefetch manifest) flows through the same emit() path but the plan does not specify which fingerprint/material_basis this non-ERROR, unpinned FAIL receives.
findings.location: Fix plan / 'Required fingerprint shape' fallback tiers; close_precheck.py:405 _emit_completion_sidecar
scenarios: A child-closure precheck FAIL is emitted: no LLM ran, so the verdict carries no plan_material_fingerprint / completion_read_basis / prefetch manifest — which basis and fingerprint does it get?
findings.suggested_fix: State that a deterministic precheck-FAIL uses current_material_fingerprint plus material_basis: "basis_unavailable" (or a dedicated 'precheck_deterministic' marker) so it is never null and is era-visibly distinct from a pinned verifier FAIL.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the consumer/reader path whose old-record tolerance the test exercises, and assert it accepts a legacy sidecar with absent material_fingerprint/verifier_version as 'unknown era' rather than rejecting it.
evidence: AC3: 'Existing sidecars are untouched (no backfill); consumers treat absent material as "unknown era".'
Scope: 'No backfill, prune, or reader rejection change; absent fields remain accepted as unknown-era records.'
Test module bullet only says 'old-record absence tolerance' — the consuming reader is not enumerated
findings.finding: AC3 asserts consumers 'treat absent material as unknown era' and the scope claims 'no reader rejection change', but the plan names no consumer/reader and no proving check that an existing reader actually tolerates a sidecar lacking material_fingerprint/verifier_version — the test module only lists 'old-record absence tolerance' without identifying which reader path is exercised.
scenarios: A consumer that newly reads material_fingerprint could throw on a legacy null record if the tolerance path is not actually exercised by a test
findings.suggested_fix: Identify the analysis/reader consumer and add an assertion that parsing a fixture sidecar missing the new fields succeeds and classifies it as unknown-era.

'Each new completion sidecar will carry a nested verifier_version object'
The consequence section notes analysis consumers ('longitudinal gate analysis version-aware') but no doc artifact is named to record the v1 schema and its fallback markers

findings.location: Fix plan > Required fingerprint shape / Required version shape
scenarios: A future analyst or maintainer needs to interpret basis_unavailable / error_unpinned markers or evolve to a _v2 fingerprint and has no captured rationale for the v1 composite shape
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short design-doc/ADR entry documenting the v1 material fingerprint composition, the verifier_version fields, and the meaning of each material_basis marker.
